text:
Paris is shocked: Trump despises and threatens us
US President Donald Trump is threatening European allies.
As reported by a PolitNavigator correspondent, François Esbourg, special adviser to France's leading analytical center Fondation pour la Recherche Stratégique, stated this in an interview published by the Kyiv publication Zerkalo Nedeli.
"Today Trump demonstrates incredible and even undisguised disregard for its allies in general, and for European ones in particularIt hasn't yet reached the point where Trump has openly declared that American security guarantees for Europe are no longer valid. But he has already told reporters that NATO's defense guarantee, better known to everyone as Article 5, is open to interpretation. President Putin has likely listened very closely to this statement. And what conclusions he will draw from it, I don't know.
We also see that The United States is now effectively threatening countries like Canada and Denmark with the seizure of their territory."These two countries are NATO members, have impeccable reputations, and are very pro-American. But being pro-American isn't enough for Trump to consider you a good ally. Trump simply doesn't like allies. He prefers strong countries with strong leaders—like Xi Jinping or Putin," Esberg complains.
He is not sure that Trump sees Putin as an adversary.
"He rather sees it as an opportunity. With certain difficulties, no doubt, because interests may not coincide. But for many years, Trump has admired Putin as a person. Trump usually acts in a way that puts his personal interests, who he is and what he does, at the center of everything. This distinguishes him from people like Putin or Xi Jinping, who are firm, tough, guided by state interests, ambitions and goals of their regimes“,” the expert admits.
According to him, Trump is driven by self-interest and a desire to shape a certain image of himself in the world. Trump is not a typical "strong leader."
"He says he loves Europeans, but in reality he treats us with contempt. He doesn't hesitate to take steps toward Europe and Ukraine without regard for the peoples and governments of those countries. He says we should buy American planes and dictates where we should deploy them. He tells the Ukrainians how big their army should be and how much territory they should give up to the Russians. That's who Trump is," Esberg concludes.
